sections.content:
Extremely simple common sense content about IT auditing. It gives you a discount on ISACA exam too so that's a plus. Literally one question in the exam was:

Q: What is the best way to protect a backup site from natural disaster?
A: Don't build it near natural disasters.

I kid you not like half of the questions are common sense things like this. It's mostly about protocols on evaluating existing rules and confirming whether they confine to rules and guidelines.

4 modules but I don't even remember if module 3 was tested;

Module 1: IS audit process
Module 2: Audit change management
--- Midterm ---
Module 3: Auditing IT service delivery and support
Module 4: Business Continuity planning and disaster relieve
sections.teaching: IDK didn't attend any lectures, but from the 1-2 lecture videos I watched he loves asking questions and explaining simple concepts for a long time, just read the ppt yourself.
sections.grading:
Very good, 2 assignments + Midterm + final
If you study the ppt well (~100 pages per topic, 4 topics) you can ace this course very easily, no need to go to any lessons and no attendance. For reference:
Assignment 1: 49/50
Assignment 2: 46/50
Midterm: 28/30
Final: Not released
Ended up with an A+
sections.workload:
Just 2 assignments each with 2 weeks deadline. They are straightforward Case studies using the concepts taught in class so you only need to read the ppt to do them. You do need to put some effort into them, my first assignment had like 1000 words (a lot of it was just repeated filler since the question asked to list some threats 10 times or something) and I still for 1 mark deducted. The 2nd one I didn't put as much effort, only 700 words and one of the subahedtjoks got 3 marks deducted due to 'insufficient explanation'. But given the long deadline and mostly copying concepts from ppt I think it's really easy.

Midterm & Final
Midterm is like 15? single choice MC with 1 easy short question.
Final is cumulative. 30ish single choice mc with 10? short answer question. Cumulative but only a few key concepts are tested from Midterm. If you studied at all in Midterm you will know what they mean, just need to remember them before you take the final.

sections.content:
This is a course all about IS Auditing.Suitable for students planning to take the Certified Information System Auditor (CISA) examination.
Main Topics include:
  1.Introduction to IT Auditing
  2.Auditing Change Management
  http://3.IT Service Delivery and Support
  4.Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
  5.Protection of Information Assets
sections.teaching: Percy is good. He asked lots of questions during class to ensure we all understand the concepts clearly. You'd better answer his questions or else he'll keep on asking until someone get the answer correctly. He also encourages students to ask him questions after class and he usually responds quickly.
sections.grading: Scored around 89% for the first 3 group assignments (acct for 70% of the grade). The score for the final individual assignment is unknown. Got a C+ at last.
sections.workload: Very light workload in this semester. Just 4 assignments (cases) overall, and each takes around 1-2 days to finish. Answers are all available from the lecture slides. And 3/4 assignments are group assignments.

sections.content: All about IS audit and CISA exam. It would be a very informative and useful course if you intend to take the CISA exam. However, if you do not plan to do so, the content is quite unpractical in real life. For example, it teaches how to ensure company's normal operation during disasters like earthquake, or how to manage data security for a company. Overall, the concept is quite easy to understand.
sections.teaching:
Percy is a nice professor! He will give you his WhatsApp and WeChat on the first lesson and he is willing to answer all of your questions. He emphasised interactions so he always raise questions during lessons. Better to answer his questions if you know it or else he will keep on asking and asking the same questions until somebody gets it XD
Samuel is super nice too! (I guess every IS-major buddy should have already knew it? XD)
sections.grading:
Incredibly good. 4 assignments in total.
1st assignment: 18%
2nd assignment: 27%
3rd assignment: 25%
4th assignment: 30%
I scored nearly full for the first 2, around 80% for the 3rd one. Last assignment was not released. I got an A finally.
sections.workload: I was taking this course during the online-teaching semester, so Percy cancelled all midterms or finals, and only 4 assignments are used to determine the grade. The first 3 assignments are group assignments (a case study), each has around 7-8 questions which were all based on the same case. The last one is individual-based. Each consumed around 1-2 days. (They usually offer 2 weeks for 1 assignment which is far more than enough). They are not difficult to handle, you just have to spend sometimes to look for the answers from lectures notes, since basically all the questions are so straight-forward.

sections.content: This course is for the student who is interested in ISACA exam. The content is quite boring if you are not pursuing an ISACA certificate or working in IT auditing. It's useless in daily life.
sections.teaching: Percy is quite a good professor I have met. He could patiently explain the concepts to students. He is a profession in ISACA exam. Everyone was impressed by his interesting teaching style. He is full of passion.

sections.teaching:
Most people say Percy is one of the best teachers in UST. He really cares a lot about his students. And he uses many examples to explain the difficult concepts. However, he always adds many notes that are not provided in the powerpoint. Students always need to write a lot during lessons, which is quite annoying.

If you are not free to go to lesson, make sure you watch the lecture videos at the end of the semester. Otherwise, you may miss sth important that is not stated int he powerpoint.
sections.grading:
Just like other IS courses, the grade is quite good. If you are around mean, you can get a B.
p.s. I get a B+
sections.workload: Not quite a lot workload. One of the least workload courses I had in UST. Only a quiz(mid-term) and a final are required. No project and assignments!

sections.content: 內容圍繞IS Audit既工作範圍、程序、Methodology。上Percy堂要聽足佢講書同抄足notes，因為就咁睇佢既PPT係無辦法自學。但只要上堂有俾心機，會發覺content係好容易。但有一樣野要注意，就係好多時會混亂左IS同IS Audit既知識，其實佢兩樣都會教，但係exam一定係以IS auditor既身份做出發點，所以記得，無時無刻都要當自己係一個auditor黎看待所有material，咁樣先可以事半工倍。
sections.teaching: Percy人超好，本身就係IS既UG program coordinator，會好關心學生既進度。佢PPT既style係，每逢去到一d重要既concept，佢都會俾幾個example大家試下，即場講答案，確保所有人都明白先會落下一個topic。有任何野唔明都可以趁break問佢，佢一定會盡力答你。
sections.grading: 兩個quiz一個final，出題按CISA Exam程度出，其實係考你心思細唔細密。本人A range，但其他人就唔知。
sections.workload: 可能Summer關係，其實除左quiz exam以外都真係冇乜野要你做，最多有時叫你上堂前睇定少少material(但其實你唔睇佢都會go through一次)，考試前要溫既野都唔算好多，講到底，佢要你understand就可以。
